dundee.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across Dundee
s1loc: Dundee and Angus Foodbank, one of the busiest in the Trussell network, runs emergency food and a community cafe from its warehouse and centres across the city, while FareShare Tayside and Fife moves surplus food from the trade out to community groups. Dundee Volunteer and Voluntary Action on Constitution Road supports the wider third sector, links volunteers to projects and keeps a list of local Tayside trusts. The big food-redistribution and foodbank networks and many small mutual-aid projects all draw helpers across this Tayside city.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying alongside hospice and community fundraising, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Lochee, Hilltown and Whitfield. We are set up to serve the national charity with shops on every high street and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the big buyers and direct online ordering, no minimum, for the smallest group.

ipswich.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across Ipswich
s1loc: FIND, short for Families in Need, has run free food parcels and household essentials from Ipswich for more than thirty years, alongside FoodCycle community meals and a network of pantries and larders. FareShare East Anglia is based in the town and moves surplus food from the trade out to charities across Suffolk, while the Suffolk Community Foundation backs local groups and St Elizabeth Hospice fundraises through its shops. The big food-redistribution and foodbank networks and many small volunteer-run projects all draw helpers across this Suffolk town.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying alongside hospice and community fundraising, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Chantry, Whitton and Gainsborough. We are set up to serve the national charity with shops on every high street and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the big buyers and direct online ordering, no minimum, for the smallest group.

In Ipswich, FIND (Families in Need) has offered a lifeline for over thirty years from Braziers Wood Road, distributing more than 5,000 food parcels a year plus furniture and bedding, sorted and delivered by an army of over eighty volunteers. The Ipswich Community Resource Centre adds welfare-benefits advice, a low-cost cafe and practical help for homeless and marginalised people, and Suffolk Community Foundation channels grants into grassroots groups. From Whitton and Chantry to the Gainsborough estate, local volunteers carry the load.
